messages.subject: geom_text legend without "A"
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to produce a plot with geom_text() with colour aesthetic
mappings, but would like to avoid the "a" in the legend. However, it has
become impossible to change it to something else (fill, coloured text,...).

This has been asked before in
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/ab2a8210eec0be21

The solution in 2009 was to simply remove the legend. In the thread
somebody mentions that it is against the idea of the grammar of graphics
(although I would appreciate if somebody can give me a reason for that),
and that Hadley was working for a solution in the future. Does anybody
knows whether the solution has been implemented?

My suggestion would be to simply have the text in the legend, with
different colours for each label, and to avoid the box with the 'a'.

-----8<---------------

x <- rnorm(10)
y <- rnorm(10)
z <- gl(2, 5)
w <- letters[1:10]
d <- data.frame(x, y, z, w)

ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_text(aes(label=w, colour=z))

-----8<---------------



Thank you,
--
- Xavier -

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: geom_text legend without "A"
parts:
> My suggestion would be to simply have the text in the legend, with
> different colours for each label, and to avoid the box with the 'a'.

It is impossible at the moment but it would be a good idea.
Maybe the colorlabel guide will be implemented in the future version.

Here is a (dirty) workaround:

ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_text(aes(label=w, colour=z), show_guide=FALSE) +
geom_text(aes(label = c("label A", "label B"), colour = z),
data.frame(x=1, y=c(-0.75, -1), z = factor(c(1, 2))),
show_guide=FALSE)

--
